# Zoomies

_Take and copy paste screen in 2 seconds. Rename? 3 seconds. Rename + annotate with prompt for agent? 5 seconds. Quick edit? 7? maybe 10..._

> **Requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later.** If you have an older macOS version, it is probably best to use this as a product spec and build your own. I had enough headaches with older OS versions already.
>
> Zoomies builds natively on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Intel is supported but untested because I do not have an Intel Mac.

Mac-only keyboard-first screenshot and scratchpad app for agentic coding.
Good for touchpad users too, especially if your wrist is already cooked from gaming.

Fork it, pork it, change it, rebuild it. Have fun.

## What It Does

- Captures the exact UI state you want a coding agent to understand.
- Adds quick notes/prompts to screenshots so the context travels with the image.
- Saves Zoomies edit data inside PNGs, so future reopens can edit/delete Zoomies-added arrows, text, pen strokes, shapes, pasted selections, and cut regions.
- Creates quick scratchpad notes for errors, issues, and ideas you spot in one project while your head is still in another.
- Lets you rename, annotate, save, copy, or delete without breaking coding flow.
- Reopens a selected Finder image and sends it back through the Zoomies flow.

When you edit and save a non-PNG image such as a JPEG or HEIC, Zoomies saves the
edited result as a PNG and removes the original non-PNG file.

## Quick Start

```bash
cd zoomies
swift build
swift run Zoomies
```

To build a clickable `.app`:

```bash
./scripts/build_app.sh
open dist/Zoomies.app
```

A coding agent can run that build script for you too.

### Building on an Intel Mac

Intel users should build Zoomies from source on their Intel Mac:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bald-ai/zoomies.git
cd zoomies
./scripts/build_app.sh
open dist/Zoomies.app
```

Swift automatically builds for the Mac it is running on: Apple silicon produces
an `arm64` app, while Intel produces an `x86_64` app. A universal binary is only
needed when distributing one prebuilt `.app` for both architectures; this
repository distributes source instead.

Intel support requires an Intel Mac running macOS 14 or later with Xcode 15 or
later. **I do not own an Intel Mac, so the Intel build has not been personally
tested.**

## Default Shortcuts

- `Option+Shift+4` -> area capture
- `Option+Shift+3` -> full-screen capture
- `Option+Shift+2` -> select an image in Finder, press this to edit/rename it with Zoomies
- `Option+Shift+1` -> create a scratchpad note
- `Option+Shift+5` -> start/stop screen recording (requires macOS 15)

The defaults intentionally avoid the standard macOS `Cmd+Shift` screenshot shortcuts.

You can change the main global shortcuts in Zoomies Settings. If you want to
change keybinds that are not exposed in the UI, ask your coding agent to update
the relevant shortcut code and build a new `.app` for you.

# Iceberg concept notes (`04-iceberg.html`)

Concept id: `iceberg`. Title: What is hidden beneath the surface?

## Owned files

- `work/code-views/04-iceberg.html`
- `work/code-views/04-iceberg-notes.md`

## Idea

Cutaway iceberg: **above the waterline** = human-language jobs other code asks for; **below** = useful work kept inside. Geometry is explicitly illustrative — not measured depth or quality. Teaches that a compact interface can hide substantial work, and that many small files alone are not evidence of bad structure.

## Examples (3 selectable)

| Job name | Swift piece | Why chosen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Preferences keeper | `SettingsStore` | Short tip (`load` / `update` / read settings); migration, repair, atomic JSON under water |
| Hidden notes in a PNG | `PNGMetadata` | Classic compact tip (`embed` / `extract` / size check); chunk/CRC/safety work under water |
| After-capture flow | `ScreenshotWorkflowController` | Everyday tip from `ScreenshotService` is `start` / `cancel`; panels, backup, persistence, metadata orchestration under water |

`EditorCanvasView` was the alternate third example; not used. Mentioned in Evidence as a possible wider-tip contrast later (1916 lines in `facts.json`).

## Interactions

- Three native buttons toggle `aria-pressed` and refresh tip chips, underwater chips, and the detail panel (why / caller knowledge / agent question / filenames disclosure).
- SVG cutaway is static decoration; live content is the chip bands + detail aside.
- Parent height: `postMessage({ type:'zoomies-concept-height', id:'iceberg', height })` on load, ResizeObserver on `body`, rAF debounce.
- Helps you see / Does not tell you at bottom; Evidence `<details>` with paths and method.

## Evidence checked in source

- `SettingsStore.swift`: `load()`, `update`, `settings`, `didRepairInvalidSettingsOnLastLoad`; private legacy path `~/.screenshot_app_settings.json`, normalize/repair persist, atomic write. `AppDelegate` uses repair flag (~101).
- `PNGMetadata.swift`: public embed/extract/isPNG/pixelDimensions; private iTXt, CRC, strip Zoomies keywords. Call sites only use helpers; keyword constants unused outside the file.
- `ScreenshotWorkflowController.swift`: `start`/`cancel`/`onFinish`; private rename/note/editor, backup, wait-for-persist, final actions. Constructed in `ScreenshotService.swift`. PNG embed delegated to `WorkflowImagePersistenceLogic` → `PNGMetadata`.
- Line counts cross-checked with `work/code-views/facts.json` (2026-09-12 snapshot): SettingsStore 127, PNGMetadata 337, ScreenshotWorkflowController 1038. Listed as size context only.

## Qualified “leak” notes (not verdicts)

- Settings: callers dig into `settings` fields; repair flag is specialized caller knowledge.
- PNG: public keyword constants exist but are not used by callers today.
- Workflow: init still wires many collaborators; panel handlers are public even though the service tip is tiny.

## Limitations for parent

- Does not score depth, health, or coupling.
- Tip/mass proportions are drawn, not derived from LOC.
- Functional groups are inferred roles in one app target.
- iframe-only: no shared nav; id must be `iceberg` for height messages.

## Parent checks

1. iframe `src` points at `04-iceberg.html`; accept height messages only when `id === 'iceberg'`.
2. Click all three examples; confirm detail + chips update and height postMessage fires.
3. Narrow ~340px: no horizontal overflow; stack stage columns.
4. Keyboard: buttons and `<summary>` show focus rings.
5. No network/font/package dependencies.

from html.parser import HTMLParser
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('/Users/applelevne/Documents/coding-projects/zoomies/work/code-views/04-iceberg.html')
text = p.read_text()
class Checker(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.errors = []
        self.stack = []
        self.void = {'meta','link','br','hr','img','input','source','area','base','col','embed','param','track','wbr'}
    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag not in self.void:
            self.stack.append(tag)
    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag in self.void:
            return
        if not self.stack:
            self.errors.append(f'unexpected </{tag}>')
            return
        if self.stack[-1] != tag:
            # allow implicit close for common cases
            if tag in self.stack:
                while self.stack and self.stack[-1] != tag:
                    self.stack.pop()
                if self.stack:
                    self.stack.pop()
            else:
                self.errors.append(f'mismatch </{tag}> stack={self.stack[-5:]}')
        else:
            self.stack.pop()
c = Checker()
c.feed(text)
print('bytes', len(text.encode()))
print('stack remaining', c.stack)
print('errors', c.errors)
# required contract checks
need = [

]

    # id check flexible

# no external deps

print('gradient count', text.count('gradient'))
